bull.b: The merger and concurrent financing could provide substantial capital to advance clinical programs through multiple development milestones. This strengthens near-term operating runway and replaces NextCure’s narrow oncology focus with access to Avere’s oral IL-23 platform and broader inflammation pipeline.

An incoming leadership team with experience advancing a biotechnology company from pre-IPO development to a major strategic sale may improve execution and capital allocation. That background is relevant as the combined company manages clinical readouts, financing, and the transition into inflammation.

Exiting the Beltsville facility eliminates ongoing rent obligations and consolidates the company’s real-estate footprint. Although the termination required a one-time payment, the recurring cost reduction can help preserve capital and align infrastructure with the company’s substantially smaller operating structure.

bear.b: NextCure has not established a commercial revenue base, while recurring operating losses show that current activities do not fund the business. Without product revenue, future value remains dependent on clinical progress, financing access, and the eventual success of development programs.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow means the company is not self-funding and must continue relying on external capital or strategic transactions. This reduces financial flexibility and makes the ability to maintain development spending sensitive to financing conditions and corporate execution.

The proposed ownership reset leaves existing NextCure shareholders with only a small economic stake in the combined company. Even with contingent value rights, this substantially reduces their participation in future upside and reflects the degree to which financing and strategy are being funded through dilution.
